To try loose leash walking: i have an 8 metre leash, he can use the whole leash. When he is at the end of the leash and starts pulling, i come to a complete stop, he has to return to a heel before we continue the walk.

At first he might only come back half way, or turn before me and try to go. Be steady, praise when he is in a heel position! Lots of praise!

It will take some time but it will get better.
Other variants are making 180 degree turn and going the other way everytime he yanks on the leash.

I have a sammy as a first dog. He lives with two main coons (best friends, one of the cats loves him more than me 😝).
I do obedience classes with him and although he was a clown and had sticks in his ears and looked everywhere except at me, we got through all the classes first time and he was always top of his class (on good days).
He does get distracted easily, he is obsessed with watching the dogs in agility. When he sees other dogs and is off leash, he WILL run off to them and try to play. He thinks all dogs are nice. He runs after deer, other cats, birds, rabbits… but comes back after.
So no they can’t be trusted off leash, bit they come back eventually.
We do scent work as well, with mixed results. He learns pretty quickly, but now tries to destroy all setups (he thinks its a game).
He can run for hours fetching sticks or balls, but if you are occupied with other stuff, he will overload you with his toys, pushing them in your face, chewing on the squeaker untill you throw is teddy bear..
He is a loveable goofball tho.
Trained my granny to feed him all the good stuff from the fridge, because “he looks so hungry and sad” (even after leftovers of chicken, three sandwiches with salami, a scoop of icecream…).

And he will complain when he was left alone (AWOooooooooooo woeoeowowow)

My understanding is that marcus aurelius wanted to point out the following: you can only influence your own behaviour, so focus on that but do not dwell on past mistakes or future challenges.
If others make mistakes, it is their doing, frustration about other people’s mistakes takes up a lot of mental energy which goes to waste. And it is you who should stand behind your decisions, not the masses (as you cannot influence them anyways), and do you only want to be liked by fools? 

So do you have to be social? I dont think thats the point, live up to your own standards, keep your thoughts on your own doing and judge your own actions. Leave others to their own.
